comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value table footnotes regarding NAV exclusion and netting
comparisons.peer_summary: Footnotes to the fair value tables indicate that amounts exclude investments measured at net asset value (NAV), specifically $23 million and $25 million in the respective reporting periods, in accordance with ASU 2015-07. Additionally, footnote (1) explains that certain values represent netting of securities repurchase/resale agreements and derivative exposures covered by qualifying master netting agreements.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and C disclose the inclusion of investments measured at Net Asset Value (NAV) within their equity securities or investment portfolios. C explicitly excludes these NAV investments from the fair value tables and provides specific amounts ($23 million and $25 million) for the periods, whereas GS includes them in the equity securities line item without providing a specific dollar amount or exclusion note in this sentence.

comparisons.peer_topic: Practical Expedient for Investments Measured at NAV
comparisons.peer_summary: Certain investments, including hedge funds, private equity, and real estate funds with fair values of $1.0 billion as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, are measured using net asset value per share as a practical expedient and are not required to be classified in the fair value hierarchy, primarily reported in other assets.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM disclose investments in private equity, real estate, and hedge funds that are measured using Net Asset Value (NAV) as a practical expedient. Both companies report a similar aggregate fair value for these NAV-measured investments ($1.0 billion for JPM). However, JPM explicitly notes these amounts are 'primarily reported in other assets' and excludes them from the fair value hierarchy, whereas GS simply lists them as part of equity securities at fair value without specifying the balance sheet line item in this specific sentence.

sentences.text: • Equity securities, at fair value includes investments in private equity, real estate and hedge funds that are measured at NAV.

At both December 31, 2024 and 2023, the fair values of these investments, which include certain hedge funds, private equity funds, real estate and other funds, were $1.0 billion, primarily reported in other assets.

comparisons.peer_topic: Measurement and liquidity characteristics of private fund investments
comparisons.peer_summary: Investments in Private Equity, Other, and Real Estate funds are measured based on Net Asset Value (NAV) and are generally not redeemable due to their closed-end nature, with distributions received only upon disposal of underlying investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS disclose that their equity securities include investments in private equity, real estate, and other funds measured at NAV. MS provides additional detail on the liquidity characteristics, stating these funds are generally not redeemable due to their closed-end nature, while GS does not mention liquidity restrictions in this specific disclosure. MS also specifies that 'Other' funds include private credit, hedge funds, etc., which overlaps with GS's 'hedge funds' category.
